Summary: Apollinarianism taught in the 4th century that Christ had a human body and soul but that the divine Logos replaced his human mind. It sought to protect Christ's sinlessness and unity.
Beliefs: Christ had no human rational mind; The Logos took the place of Christ's human mind; Christ was not fully human in mind
Controversy: Condemned at the Council of Constantinople AD 381; Gregory of Nazianzus argued what is not assumed is not healed
ChristianResponse: The church affirmed that Jesus assumed full humanity, including a human mind, to redeem the whole person, citing Hebrews 2:17 and Luke 2:52.
